entities.summary:
Marcus Titius was a Roman politician and commander at the end of the Roman Republic.

He served as the consul in 48 BCE, but his career was marked by controversy and scandal. The Senate stripped him of his legions in 44 BCE, and he was later defeated by Mark Antony at the Battle of Philippi in 42 BCE.

Despite these setbacks, Titius continued to play a significant role in Roman politics, serving as a senator until his death in 1 BCE. His legacy is still debated among historians today.
